companion case to roth v. united states

This chunk is about:
- Events: Miller v. California, Gates v. Collier, Roth v. United States
- Organizations: United States Supreme Court, Fifth Circuit
- Systems: Trusty system (prison)
- Places: Mississippi
- Concepts: Obscenity, First Amendment, prison reform

Facts:
- Roth v. United States, 354 U.S. 476 (1957), was a United States Supreme Court case about the constitutional test for obscene material unprotected by the First Amendment.
- Miller v. California, 413 U.S. 15 (1973), was a landmark United States Supreme Court decision that redefined obscenity from material "utterly without socially redeeming value" to material lacking serious literary, artistic, political, or scientific value.
- The page text says Roth v. United States was described along with Miller v. California as redefining the constitutional test for obscenity.
- Gates v. Collier, 501 F.2d 1291 (5th Cir.), was identified as the Gates v. Collier Prison Reform Case of 1970–1971.
- Gates v. Collier ended flagrant abuse of inmates under the trusty system and other prison abuses in Mississippi that had continued essentially unchanged since the prison was built in 1903.
